now_the_spec_says: A probe's pointer is a FILE PATH, not an id: the path is the link, the filesystem is the index, no receiver resolves anything. by_copy narrows to a receiver that cannot read that filesystem, else it goes. An intention owns its tickets; self-ownership gates nothing.

reading_correction.what_was_wrong: Both prior packets listed these files under what_dies. ruling.py reads what_dies as LITERAL DELETION — its verify prints 'STILL ALIVE: <path> was ruled dead and is on disk' — so confirming either packet would have made 'delete cairn/base/probe.py', a file eight live modules import, a green instruction. His four verbatim lines sentence nothing: re-read against the nine paths on 2026-08-06, not one of them names a file to remove. what_dies had been populated with every file the ruling TOUCHES, and those are not the same list.
reading_correction.why_the_slip_had_nowhere_else_to_go: what_conforms went green only when a file's bytes changed since the packet's own intake, which assumed the paperwork precedes the work. These packets were opened at 15:39 and 15:56 and the work landed at 16:05 in commit 5ae26b9 — so at intake nothing had moved yet, and what_dies was the only field that could ever have gone green. The gate's shape pushed toward the wrong field. Fixed the same day: `as_of` names the commit the ruling was made against, git renders the file as it stood then, and the door fingerprints THAT.
reading_correction.what_changed_besides_the_field: The commit touched TEN files; the first packet named eight, the second nine. cairn/base/proofs/test_does_optional_probe.py was in neither. It is here.
reading_correction.claude_md_dropped_on_purpose: Both prior packets put cairn/CLAUDE.md under what_conforms and both reported it UNTOUCHED. Checked 2026-08-06: CLAUDE.md says nothing about probes, pointers or carriers, and its Law 6 line ('everything has exactly one owner') was already true and is unchanged by 'an intention owns its tickets'. Nothing in it was ever owed. It is dropped rather than carried forward as a red nobody can ever clear.
reading_correction.the_conformance_is_proven_not_asserted: The byte-changed check says the files moved, never that they moved correctly — verify says so itself. The real proof is cairn/base/proofs/test_probe_carry.py, 17/17 green under the tester, whose teeth are the carriage behaviours the ruling names.
reading_correction.gate_still_owed: Nothing checks a what_dies list at intake. A grep for importers of each dying path, refusing a packet that sentences a file the corpus still imports, is the physics this correction is the hand-run version of — Law 4. Filed at troubles/what-dies-sentences-files-the-corpus-still-imports.

confirmation_verbatim: as long as there isn't a better more inspectable approach than that. [CC checked before confirming: the only alternative is an id plus a resolver, and a resolver is a registry, which is settled dead (no-enforcer-gated-ownership). A path is inspectable with ls/cat/git — tools that already exist and cannot disagree with the truth. An id is inspectable only THROUGH its resolver, a second thing that can be wrong and that nothing inspects.]

supersedes.evidence: what_dies named nine live files including cairn/base/probe.py, which eight modules import; ruling.py reads what_dies as literal deletion. Akien's four verbatim lines sentence nothing. Root cause measured: what_conforms went green only on bytes changed since INTAKE, and this packet was opened before the work landed, so what_dies was the only field that could ever have gone green.

Same defect as its own predecessor: the rescope corrected the READING (by_copy) but carried the nine-file what_dies list forward untouched, plus CLAUDE.md as a permanently-UNTOUCHED conformer. The corrected packet empties what_dies, adds the tenth file the commit touched, and drops CLAUDE.md, which was never owed.
